description.p: Stack is an independent document library for the COSMIC desktop. Import documents, organize them into stacks, search printed English text offline, and keep saved changes in sync with an approved nearby Android phone.
Documents are stored locally. No account or cloud service is required.

Documents your partner shares with you now appear in search and the document list, marked "Shared by" their name. Opening the original still happens on the phone. Stack updates its library to a newer format the first time you open this version, so install it on every computer you use.

Installing Stack is now one step: the package sets up its own updates. Opening a linked document no longer warns when the file has the same name and was only edited since. A second start says Stack is already open.
The version number is now always visible in the window title, for example "Stack 0.6.2 — All documents". 0.6.1 only showed it inside the Backup & restore menu.
The window now shows which version of Stack you have, next to the Backup key line.
Stack is now installed as a normal program (a .deb) and updates arrive through the system updater. Open in Ami Pro starts Ami Pro directly. The library, pairing and backup key are unchanged.

The backup key can now be saved on desktops whose portal has no secret store, such as COSMIC, using the login keyring. The Backup key tooltip shows where the key is stored. Keys saved by 0.5.0 are still found.

Stack links between documents now sync with the phone. The saved backup key is kept in the app's own data folder and is carried over from the old place, and key handling no longer hangs when the computer's secret store is slow or locked.
Open a stack and see the other stacks that share its documents, for example Bills inside House. Tap one to show only the shared documents.

Updates now arrive through your app store or flatpak update. Pairing certificates are created inside Stack, phone sync uses TLS 1.3 only, and a safety copy of the library is saved before changes from the phone are applied.
Syncing with the phone uses much less processing when nothing has changed.
